description: The maximum possible nameplate capacity for offshore wind development is 26,800 GW.
context_quote: The results indicate that 64% of total (61.5% of contiguous) U.S. coastal area is available for offshore wind development, translating to a maximum possible nameplate capacity of 26,800 GW.

description: Wind speed threshold for development is set at 7 m/s at a hub height of 150 m.
context_quote: The regions with the largest available areas at 150 m hub height and a 7 m/s wind speed threshold include Alaska (~1,784,300 km [2]), Hawaii (~718,600 km [2]), and the Northern California Coast (~127,000 km [2]).

description: Certain areas are restricted due to conflicting ocean uses, protected areas, or low wind speeds.
geographic_scope: Restricted areas in U.S. coastal regions
context_quote: Although all regions have some restricted areas, certain areas are especially restricted due to conflicting ocean uses, protected areas, or low wind speeds.

description: Wind farms must be located near existing or planned electrical transmission infrastructure.
geographic_scope: Near existing or planned electrical transmission infrastructure
context_quote: Furthermore, offshore wind farms should be sited away from shipping lanes, fishing grounds, and protected marine areas.

description: The proximity to suitable ports influences transportation and installation costs.
context_quote: The cost of inter-connecting the wind farm to the electrical grid depends on the distance to the nearest substation.
